title: model-arch-performance-notes-llama-mistral-qwen-moe-routing
content:
Summary:

This doc captures our recent profiling and benchmark findings for three model architectures in our runtime: Llama-family, Mistral-family, and Qwen-family, with a focus on long-context behavior and MoE routing overheads. The goal is to surface architecture-specific bottlenecks we observed on our standard inference stack (A100/80GB-ish class nodes + Triton-like serving path), quantify impact, and propose mitigations and next experiments.

Quick takeaways:
- Llama (decoder-only dense): CPU/GPU memory-bound at long seq lengths due to KV cache layout; attention softmax and GEMM dominate per-token cost for sequences > 8k.
- Mistral (lighter-weight dense with grouped linear layers): better throughput at short sequences but suffers from kernel launch overhead and suboptimal GEMM shapes at higher dims; activation memory for intermediate FFN blocks is smaller but latency jitter higher.
- Qwen (wider models, variant mix): scales poorly with naive batching at long context because of larger layer widths and increased I/O for KV cache; MoE variants show consistent routing overhead (~5-15% latency) and load imbalance unless we shard experts carefully.

Environment and tools:
- HW: NVIDIA A100 40GB / 80GB nodes for most experiments.
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime (custom kernels + cuBLAS/cuDNN fallbacks), CUDA 12.x, cuBLASLt for matmuls.
- Profilers: Nsight Systems for timeline + kernel breakdown; nvprof/cupti traces for kernels; torch.profiler for operator-level counts (model conversion path); internal token-level latency tracing in Console.
- Workloads: single-stream low-latency (batch=1), latency SLOs; high-throughput batching (batch up to 32) for offline throughput numbers; long-context experiments for seq_len = [2048, 8192, 16384].

Detailed findings by architecture:

1) Llama-family (13B/30B variants)
- KV cache layout: using [num_layers, batch, num_heads, head_dim, seq] shaped cache (our current layout) causes non-contiguous memory strides for token-append operations. Appending 1 token at a time triggers scatter/gather patterns in device memory leading to extra overhead. Timeline shows repeated small kernels for KV writes.
- Attention softmax + GEMM: For seq_len > 8k, attention GEMM (Q*K^T / scaling) and softmax kernels dominate (>60% of per-token time). cuBLAS Lt gives good throughput for large GEMMs but the shape changes at each step (growing sequence) reduce kernel reuse.
- Memory pressure: 30B models approach persistent memory limits when using long-context + batch >1. Paging not seen (with 80GB), but memory allocations cause spikes and occasional small GC-like pauses in allocator.
- Mitigations tried & results:
  - KV cache layout change -> transposed layout (grouped by head_dim inner contiguous) reduced KV write kernels by ~25% and reduced per-token latency by ~6% at seq=8192.
  - Fuse Q*K matmul + scale + softmax -> custom fused kernel reduced attention cost by ~20% on 13B, ~12% on 30B (larger models less benefited due to memory-bound behavior).

2) Mistral-family (7B and variants)
- Layer geometry: Mistral uses wider but shallower FFN shapes in parts; effective matmul shapes are often non-square which hurts cuBLAS occupancy for some sizes.
- Kernel-launch overheads: Small per-layer matmuls lead to relatively higher kernel-launch overheads for batch=1 streaming use-cases. Timeline shows many short-running kernels interleaved, leading to scheduling jitter.
- Activation memory: Lower peak working set than similarly-sized Llama variants; this helps avoid some allocator spikes.
- Mitigations tried & results:
  - Aggressive kernel fusion for small matmuls reduced kernel count by ~40%, latency improvement ~8-10% for batch=1 at seq <2048.
  - Grouped batching (micro-batching inside device) benefits amortize kernel-launch costs when batchable; however, this impacts tail latency and is only viable for best-effort endpoints.

3) Qwen-family (14B, 22B and MoE variants)
- Width and I/O: Wider layers in Qwen increase the per-token flop count and the size of the KV cache per token. For long context, this increases DRAM footprint and per-token memory traffic causing bandwidth contention.
- MoE routing cost: The gating network + top-k selection adds extra compute per token and an extra memory indirection to route activations to expert weights. Nsight timelines show the gating (softmax/top-k) as a distinct step before expert matmuls; total routing overhead measured between ~5% (when experts well-utilized) and up to ~15% (when routing imbalance causes load spikes).
- Expert load imbalance: For standard random seeds and typical prompts, some experts get overloaded causing hot spots; this results in queuing latency and increased variance.
- Mitigations tried & results:
  - Expert sharding across CUDA devices (expert per-device) reduced cross-device comms but increased variance for batch=1; for larger batches it reduced tail latency by ~12%.
  - Route caching for popular tokens: simple LRU cache of routing decisions for the last N tokens reduced gating cost by ~30% for chat-style workloads where tokens repeat; effective when cache hit rate > 40%.
  - Top-k quantized gating: using int8 routines for the gating NN gives small speedups (~6%) with negligible quality loss in preliminary tests.

Long-context specific notes:
- Sequence scaling behavior: Effective per-token cost increases roughly linearly with existing sequence length for attention-heavy parts; however, we observed super-linear small effects due to increased kernel fragmentation and allocator churn for very large seq lengths (>12k) on 40GB machines.
- KV cache strategy: Appending tokens should be O(1) where possible; any implementation that copies entire KV blocks per append will blow up. Our earlier layout did small copies — replacing with append-friendly contiguous buffers avoided repeated device-to-device memcpy and reduced overall token tail latency.
- Batching interactions: Batching helps throughput but exacerbates memory pressure for long-context and MoE models. For long-context low-latency endpoints, prefer batch=1 plus aggressive caching/batching heuristics in the router (group similar sequence-length requests temporally).

Profiling artifacts and numbers (representative):
- Llama-13B, A100 80GB, batch=1:
  - seq=2048: p50 token latency = 12.4ms, attention+GEMM ~55% of time, KV write ~8%
  - seq=8192: p50 token latency = 28.1ms, attention+GEMM ~62% of time, KV write ~14%
  - With fused softmax kernel: seq=8192 p50 = 24.5ms (~13% improvement)

- Mistral-7B, A100 40GB, batch=1:
  - seq=1024: p50 token latency = 7.1ms, kernel-launch overhead ~18% of time
  - After fusing small matmuls: p50 = 6.2ms

- Qwen-14B-MoE (4 experts) on 2x A100 pooled experts (expert sharding strategy), batch=4:
  - seq=2048: throughput ~22 tok/s/device aggregated, routing overhead ~9% of per-token time, tail 95th latency increases when expert imbalance >25%

Recommendations and next steps:
1) KV cache layout change: rollout transposed/append-friendly layout as an A/B experiment for Llama paths. Monitor memory usage and p50/p95 token latency. Expected ~5-10% p50 improvement for long-context.
2) Fused attention kernels: prioritize fused QK^T + scale + softmax kernels for Llama 13B/30B; focus on memory-bound optimizations (reduce temp buffers).
3) Mistral kernel fusion: continue work to combine sequences of small matmuls/linear+activation patterns to reduce kernel count. Add micro-batching path for non-SLO endpoints.
4) MoE routing improvements:
   - Implement route-caching layer in router with configurable cache size and TTL. Start with small cache (256-1024 entries) and measure hit rate for chat workloads.
   - Improve expert load balancer: use light-weight dynamic load estimation on device to avoid hot expert queuing (e.g., token-steering to second-best expert when load > threshold).
   - For multi-device expert deployments, prioritize colocating hot experts with high-throughput endpoints.
5) Instrumentation: add more fine-grained per-kernel counters in production traces to correlate gating/cache hit/miss with observed tail latency.
6) Quantization: expand int8 kernels for gating and some FFN blocks where accuracy impact is small; these provide consistent latency reductions on Qwen-MoE gating steps.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- How much does prefetching future KV regions (speculative) help for predictable streaming workloads? Risk: wasted work for non-followups.
- Can we build a heuristic to detect when routing cache should be bypassed (e.g., one-off tokens) to avoid stale hits?
- Evaluate expert-sparsity tradeoffs: more experts increases routing overhead but reduces per-expert size; need to quantify in our infra.

Appendix: quick links to raw traces and scripts:
- Nsight traces: s3://redwood-profiling/2025-11/llama-13b-8192-v1.timeline (internal)
- Scripts used: GH-PR-1482 contains the kernel-fuse prototype and benchmark harness.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is a working summary; some numbers are representative medians from 20-run samples and not full distributions. Please comment on proposed rollout priorities and any additional experiments you want prioritized.
